business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Company offshore regime administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority, Apia)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common-law foundation with local Samoan statutes; offshore International Company regime superimposed by the International Companies Act 1987)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, in force 13 December 2020; investment and trade facilitation with Pacific and OECD partners)
World Trade Organization Membership (Samoa acceded 10 May 2012)

No standalone bilateral investment treaty or comprehensive double taxation agreement is currently in force between Samoa and the People's Republic of China or major franchisor-origin economies; investor protection rests on the International Companies Act 1987, the Constitution of Samoa, and contractual franchise instruments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended by the Money Laundering Prevention (Amendment) Act 2013; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2013; International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, including the registered agent record-keeping obligations, register of members and directors, and the requirement to hold beneficial ownership particulars with the licensed registered agent in Samoa; International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019; Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit AML/CFT Guidelines issued pursuant to the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; Samoa's Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering mutual evaluation commitments; United Nations Security Council sanctions implementation framework applicable in Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport of each beneficial owner, director, and shareholder holding 25% or more (certified within the last 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Samoan Honorary Consulate in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa is a Contracting Party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961; apostille certificates are issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Apia; consular legalization is not required for Apostille member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within the last 90 days) for each beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or issuing local authority/utility entity in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Samoa; consular legalization only if the originating state is not an Apostille Contracting Party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the originating bank confirming account standing and source of funds for each significant beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the Samoan diplomatic post having competence if the originating state is not an Apostille Contracting Party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, constitutional documents, and register of directors of the ultimate parent company of the boba tea franchise chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization in non-Apostille jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT individual due diligence questionnaire, source-of-wealth statement, and beneficial ownership declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SIFA-licensed registered agent in Samoa (notarization discretionary, internal retention mandatory)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal registered agent record; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List, and Samoa FIU and domestic regulatory lists, plus adverse media and politically exposed person (PEP) database checks at onboarding and on a continuous risk-based basis thereafter; PEP classification requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and source-of-funds documentation on all franchise royalty and syrup supply payments; the licensed registered agent must maintain a written CDD file for a minimum of five years under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, as amended.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Corporate Registry — name search, clearance, and reservation system administered by the Registrar of International Companies; applications are submitted exclusively through SIFA-licensed registered agents in Apia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names of International Companies must be recorded in English using the Latin (Roman) alphabet; Samoan-language components are permitted provided they are rendered in Latin script. No mandatory transliteration or local script requirement applies to the offshore International Company regime. The name must terminate with a corporate designator such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Corp.' or 'Inc.', and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name on the Registrar's index, nor import a false connection with the Government of Samoa, a domestic Samoan company, or a regulated financial institution.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 calendar days of a written refusal by the Registrar of International Companies, the applicant's licensed registered agent may lodge a formal reconsideration request with the Registrar at SIFA, attaching written submissions distinguishing the proposed name from registered names and demonstrating that any sensitive token is not misleading; if the Registrar upholds the refusal, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the Minister responsible for the International Companies Act within a further 21 calendar days, whose decision on review is final; an entirely new name application may be filed immediately without penalty and does not require a fresh reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A standalone virtual office does not satisfy the statutory requirement; every International Company must at all times maintain a registered office being a physical street address in Samoa, normally the office of the SIFA-licensed registered agent in Apia, accessible during business hours. The boba tea franchise licensing, royalty, and syrup supply chain management may be conducted remotely by non-resident directors, but the registered office and registered agent obligations remain anchored in Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 5-10% annualized risk of an unannounced physical inspection directed at the International Company itself; materially higher inspection probability applies to the licensed registered agent's office and client due diligence records under SIFA's compliance monitoring cycle and Samoa's Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering follow-up reporting. Inspections of the remote franchise operations outside Samoa are not within domestic regulatory reach at this stage.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed-fee advisory engagement for a low-risk franchise licensing structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing international courier rate for expedited document delivery to Apia

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 4–10 (incorporation), s. 65 (registered office), ss. 74 and 79 (directors & secretary), s. 96 (tax exemptions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form A – Application for Incorporation of an International Company (with attached Memorandum & Articles of Association, statutory declarations, and consent of registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; at least one share may be issued and may remain unpaid, and no escrow deposit is required prior to incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers' subscription for the Beneficial Share(s) be approved and the allotment of shares be completed, subject to receipt of full consideration. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office at [insert Samoan address] of Samoa International Finance Authority, as notified by the registered agent, be and is hereby adopted as the company's registered office, and the registered agent is authorized to act under the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] and [Name] be appointed as Director(s) and [Name] as Secretary, each consenting to act. RATIFYING all acts already done on behalf of the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through a licensed Samoan registered agent or directly to the SIFA registry, specifying two proposed company names in order of preference. Await electronic confirmation of availability and reservation, which is valid for 180 days.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of passport or other official ID for each proposed subscriber
Proof of registered agent engagement instruction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file a revised reservation with an alternative name that distinguishes from existing entities; appeal to the Registrar within 14 days if refusal is alleged to be erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoan Registered Agent under the oversight of SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the registered agent to prepare draft constitutional documents in English, including authorized share capital, share classes, directors' powers, indemnity clauses, and a restricted-objects clause. Verify that the draft includes the required declaration under the International Companies Act 1987 concerning the company's proposed activities and absence of domestic trading. Circulate drafts for sponsor and beneficial owner review and notarization if required by the agent.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association draft
Proposed share structure and subscriber details
KYC documents (certified passport, bank reference, business plan)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The agent will revise drafts to incorporate regulator comments; final versions are re-certified by a Samoan notary public before submission if the registry raises clarifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of Incorporation Application with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Form A together with the final Memorandum and Articles of Association, registered agent consent, notice of registered office, and prescribed government fee. File may be submitted through SIFA's e-portal or in person at the Samoa International Finance Authority office. Pay the official state filing fee of USD 100 and the registered agent's service fee.
required_dossiers: Notice of registered office in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, address the specific requisition within 15 business days by filing a supplementary affidavit or letter; request an extension if additional due diligence is required, or withdraw and resubmit after deficiency cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and allocates a unique registration number in the Register of International Companies. The certificate includes the company name, date of incorporation, and language of the constitutional documents. The registered agent retrieves the certificate and authentic copies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, file a request for rectification with the Registrar; the company may apply to the Registry for a restated certificate upon payment of a nominal amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent / Board of Directors (recorded at the SIFA registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to ratify share allotment, adopt the registered office, appoint directors and secretary, approve initial corporate bank account signatories, and authorize company seal. Prepare and file minutes of the first board meeting and notify the Registrar of the names and addresses of directors and secretary within the statutory time period.
required_dossiers: Consent to act forms from directors and secretary
Notice of director and secretary appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any irregularity in the minutes or appointments is cured by passing a ratification resolution at a subsequent board meeting and filing a corrective notice with SIFA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exempt Status and Post-Incorporation Compliance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) in coordination with Ministry of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal election for tax exemption under the International Companies Act 1987, and obtain an exemption certificate confirming that the company's franchise royalties and syrup supply chain revenue are free from Samoan income tax and withholding taxes. Also register with the Samoan tax authority if any local payroll or GST obligations arise, though the IC is generally exempt.
required_dossiers: Declaration of tax exempt status election
Registered agent certificate of ongoing legal presence
Annual fee payment for licence under SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the exemption is challenged, submit a written position to the Ministry of Revenue with reference to the exclusive exemption provisions of the International Companies Act 1987, and request direct registry-to-tax authority confirmation to cure ambiguous status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Business Licensing Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 2008 (Samoa) – covering franchise licensing, wholesale of beverage syrups, and associated import/export stockholding; for an International Company, a restricted activity licence is required only if local physical operations are established

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) – Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier 2 – Environmental Registration for small-scale syrups mixing and bottling (< 500 tonnes/year); Full EIA Report required for manufacturing facilities above 500 tonnes/year or those located within a sensitive catchment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge: pH 6.0–9.0, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 250 mg/L, TSS ≤ 70 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L per Samoa Water Authority standards; volatile organic compounds (VOCs) ≤ 10 mg/m³ at vent stack; hazardous wastes segregated and disposed at an approved landfill

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFEESA) for premises; structural safety clearance under the Samoa National Building Code issued by PUMA; occupational safety and health compliance certified by MCIL following Ministry of Health inspection for food-grade storage and personnel handling

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa, Samoa Tax Administration; electronic return and registration portal: Ministry of Revenue e-Services (revenue.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Samoa International Company with the International Companies Registry and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and the International Company Tax Exemption Certificate. Step 2: If the IC will make taxable supplies in Samoa or voluntarily seeks to recover input VAGST, submit a TIN application and VAGST registration application to the Ministry of Revenue using the IC registration number, certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, certified identity documents for directors and shareholders, registered office address, and, if applicable, a local tax representative. Step 3: The Ministry of Revenue validates the application and issues a Samoa TIN / VAGST registration number. Non-resident foreign entities must use an approved tax representative in Samoa and provide apostilled or legalized documents in English. An IC that remains strictly offshore is not compellable to register for a domestic tax or VAT ID; the International Company registration number serves as the statutory identifier for banking and corporate purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: A qualifying Samoa International Company is a separate juridical entity that is not a pass-through and is statutorily treated as offshore tax-exempt. All foreign-source income, gains, distributions, and international business activities of the IC are exempt from Samoa income tax and withholding tax. The exemption is territorial and conditional upon the IC not carrying on domestic business in Samoa; any local-source business activity may trigger ordinary entity-level income taxation and forfeiture or restriction of the tax-exempt status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box election and has no explicit hybrid-mismatch check-the-box regime. The only relevant statutory elections are: (i) the IC's application for and retention of the International Company Tax Exemption Certificate; (ii) voluntary conversion from International Company status to an ordinary domestic company, which ends the Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment; and (iii) voluntary registration for VAGST as an exporter in order to recover input tax while preserving income tax exemption. No group registration, fiscal unity, or consolidated filing election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST), administered by the Samoa Ministry of Revenue under the Goods and Services Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (Samoan tala) of taxable supplies in any continuous 12-month period; compulsory registration applies at this threshold, and voluntary registration is available for exporters and other persons carrying on taxable activities
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently impose mandatory real-time Government fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping for invoices. A registered VAGST person must issue a compliant tax invoice containing the supplier's name and VAGST number, recipient details, date, description of supply, taxable amount, and VAGST charged. Returns are filed through the Ministry of Revenue e-Services portal, while Customs export declarations are processed through the ASYCUDA customs system. No pre-approval or government clearance of individual commercial invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered IC may apply 0% VAGST only to direct exports of goods or to genuine offshore supplies of services. Goods must be physically exported from Samoa to a foreign destination within the prescribed period, with the risk and benefit in the goods passing to a non-resident purchaser. Offshore services, including international franchise licensing and royalty supplies, are zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident franchisee and the rights granted are used wholly outside Samoa. Supplies to Samoan domestic consumers, local franchisees, or local physical retail outlets remain subject to 15% VAGST. The exemption also does not authorize zero-rating if the IC remains outside the VAGST net; zero-rating is a VAGST-registered exporter mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration validated by the Samoa Customs Service
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Sea Waybill showing the Samoa supplier as exporter and the foreign consignee
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Foreign currency sale contract, franchise agreement, or purchase order evidencing the cross-border supply
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 bank credit evidencing receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Certificate of Origin where required by Samoa Customs or the destination customs authority
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to heightened audit scrutiny, particularly for related-party franchise royalty and syrup supply chains. The Ministry of Revenue may reverse a zero-rating determination where the documentation is incomplete, the goods did not physically leave Samoa, the services were consumed or enjoyed in Samoa, or the transaction lacks commercial substance. In such cases all output VAGST becomes payable at 15%, previously credited input VAGST is clawed back, and interest and statutory late-payment and shortfall penalties accrue from the original due date. Fraudulent export or refund claims may lead to criminal prosecution, monetary penalties, imprisonment of responsible directors, suspension or revocation of VAGST registration, forfeiture of customs bonds, and possible loss of the International Company tax-exempt status. Registered exporters must retain the full export evidence bundle for at least six years from the date of supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) — administering exchange control under the Exchange Control Act 1972 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1975 (as amended); all foreign exchange transactions require CBS general or specific authority, exercised through licensed authorized dealer banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed-float regime with full current-account convertibility for documented trade and service transactions, while capital-account convertibility is restricted. Current-account settlements require underlying contracts/invoices routed through authorized dealers. Capital inflows, including equity injections and intra-group loans, require a Foreign Investment Certificate under the Foreign Investment Act 2020 and CBS exchange control authorization. Profit and dividend remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted after final dividend withholding tax, audited financial statements, tax clearance, and dividend declaration are submitted; practical hurdles include documentary substantiation, limited WST market depth, and CBS approval of the foreign-currency payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from the franchise syrup supply chain and royalty-related exports must be repatriated to a licensed Samoan bank within 3 months from the date of shipment under the Exchange Control Regulations 1975. The full FOB value of goods exported must be received in Samoa unless an approved deduction applies. Receipts must be surrendered and converted into WST through an authorized dealer upon credit, unless the CBS grants prior approval to maintain a foreign-currency account. Any shortfall or delayed remittance must be justified with documentary evidence, such as proof of defective goods, re-export, or commercial dispute settlements, to avoid exchange control penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Samoa (merged entity of National Bank of Samoa and Samoa Commercial Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operational Royalty Sweep Account
Operational Account + Trade Settlement LC Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Offshore digital EMIs cannot independently serve as settlement providers in Samoa; under the Financial Institutions Act 2016 (as amended), any entity issuing e-money or providing payment services must hold a CBS license. A foreign EMI may operate only as a front-end collection gateway that settles into a CBS-licensed bank account. Standalone use is blocked by licensing, local presence, and AML/CFT supervision requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person onboarding is the default standard: at least one director or a designated senior authorized signatory must attend a compliance interview physically, either at the Samoan bank branch or at a recognized offshore branch of the same banking group. Fully remote account opening is permitted only on a case-by-case basis upon compliance committee approval, supported by apostilled corporate documents, video-call verification, and notarized certified copies. Notarized copies alone do not substitute for the interview mandate without senior approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity — trust-based ownership, nominee directors, and zero-tax International Company status raising FATF-style source of wealth scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation and IC register, full register of shareholders and beneficial owners, trust deed and trustee resolution, settlor/protector profile, source-of-wealth statements, and a group structure chart evidencing commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Franchise royalty model — recurring cross-border passive payments to the Samoa IC treated as potential royalty-based money-laundering layering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly registered master franchise agreements and sub-franchise registrations, registered trademark and IP title certificates, royalty calculation schedules, supporting invoice trail, audited financial statements, and prior-period tax clearances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Syrups/concentrate supply chain — related-party import trading with high-risk counterparty jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Arm's-length supply contracts, commercial invoices, bills of lading, customs entries, transfer pricing documentation, and know-your-supplier files maintained by the corporate compliance unit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Secure a Foreign Investment Certificate under Samoa's Foreign Investment Act 2020 and CBS exchange control approval before wiring. Route the equity or intra-group loan via SWIFT MT103 from a non-resident remitter into a CBS-licensed bank account, applying the IMF BPM6 purpose classification of 'Direct investment — equity' or 'Other investment — intra-group loan' in the receiving bank's repatriation coding. The remitter must transmit the board resolution, share allocation ledger, source-of-funds evidence, and a written instruction to the receiving bank for CBS Exchange Control declaration. Verification on receipt includes remitter identity, alignment with the FIC, and compliance with International Company capital maintenance guidance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and approved royalty disbursements, presenting underlying invoices and the CBS exchange control declaration; use commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) for concentrate and syrup imports when transacted through Bank of Samoa or BSP Samoa correspondent USD clearing against an approved credit facility. All outgoing payments require valid tax clearance, contractual support, and the CBS general authority for genuine trade and service transactions; no balance-of-payments restriction applies to documented merchandise and service payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed via international banks outside Samoa
Deliverable spot and forward contracts with licensed Samoan authorized dealer banks
Cross-currency swaps subject to CBS-specific approval and documentary evidence of economic substance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year, covering status as of the preceding 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee USD 50 for the first month and USD 100 per additional month; persistent non-filing triggers administrative dissolution after 6 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Renewal Fee / Certificate of Good Standing Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation, but must be paid by 30 June to maintain listing in the active register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Strike-off notice after 3 months of arrears; reinstatement payable with penalty plus court/registrar restoration fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa registered agent and, upon request, the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June; within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to WST 50,000 and liability for directors; confers non-compliance status on the registered agent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Licence / Trading Certificate Renewal (Franchise Licensing Activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour - Business Licensing Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewable in January of each year; overdue after 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Liability fee of 10% of unpaid licence fees per month; operating without a valid licence is a criminal offence subject to WST 10,000 fine

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a tax-exempt International Company under the Samoa International Companies Act 1987; audit may be required by special resolution of members, by court order, or if the company conducts business with Samoan residents or holds land in Samoa
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or local Generally Accepted Accounting Practice, as adopted for the company's internal statutory records; no public filing requirement

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each International Company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and submit an annual confirmation to its retained registered agent by 30 June. The confirmation must list all ultimate beneficial owners, changes in shareholding, directorships, and indemnity rights. Registers are not filed publicly but must be available at the registered office for inspection by the Registrar or Financial Intelligence Unit.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 - 3,500 where audit is voluntarily undertaken

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — Samoa International Companies (ICs) are statutorily exempt under the International Companies Act 1987 from all Samoan income tax on offshore business income. The general resident corporate income tax rate under the Income Tax Act 2012 is 27%, which does not attach to IC franchise royalty, syrup supply, or trademark licensing income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax exemption, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax on distributions, and no Samoan VAT (VAGST) on IC offshore activities. The only recurring fiscal charge is the annual SIFSA license fee, graduated by authorized share capital and remitted through the licensed registered agent. A boba tea global franchisor holding brand and supply-chain contracts in the Samoa IC therefore achieves a 0% effective Samoan tax rate provided the offshore-scope and economic substance requirements are continuously met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoan corporate income tax return is filed by a tax-exempt International Company. The sole annual filing obligation is the IC Annual Confirmation Statement (SIFSA Form IC-AC) under the International Companies Act 1987, filed electronically through the SIFSA online registry by the licensed Samoan registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation; the annual license fee must be paid concurrently for the upcoming year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 — Company Name and IC Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name and unique International Company number as recorded on the certificate of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The offshore franchisor must match the name exactly to the registered English or Chinese name; discrepancies trigger registry objections and bank KYC failures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 — Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical Samoan registered office address and the name and licence number of the Samoan registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must not list a foreign address as the registered office; the Samoan agent's address governs service of process and tax notices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, and appointment dates of each director and the secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A minimum of one director, whether individual or corporate and non-resident, is permitted; nominee directors must declare their status and the ultimate beneficial owner must be disclosed to the agent for AML purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Authorized and Issued Share Capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number, class, par value, and aggregate authorized and issued capital; details of each shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital applies; bearer shares are prohibited; the beneficial shareholder schedule must remain in Samoa at the registered agent's office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Short description of the business, e.g., 'Franchise licensing, trademark royalties, and supply chain management for boba tea operations (ISIC 5610).'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The description must remain offshore-facing and must not indicate Samoan-source trading, Samoan landholding, or services to Samoan residents, which would breach the IC licence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of whether the company carries on a relevant activity (intellectual property holding, distribution and service centre, headquarters, financing and leasing, etc.) and whether it is managed and controlled in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A boba franchise royalty holder is an IP relevant activity; the declaration must be supported by board minutes evidencing Samoan meetings, local substance premises, and local staff records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 — Declaration of No Samoa-Source Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that no income was derived from sources within Samoa and that no business was conducted with Samoan residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: False certification is a criminal offence; any inadvertent sale to a Samoan consumer through local POS rails must be remediated before the confirmation statement is signed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: SIFSA late fee of WST 500 plus WST 50 per day of default; the annual license fee accrues a 10% late penalty and 2% monthly compounding interest. Persistent non-filing triggers automatic suspension, a reinstatement charge of approximately WST 5,000, and eventual striking-off and deregistration of the IC without discharging director or shareholder liabilities.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — dividends and other distributions paid by a Samoa International Company to non-resident shareholders are outside the Samoan tax net. For ordinary resident companies the Income Tax Act 2012 imposes a final non-resident dividend withholding tax of 15%, but this is not levied on IC distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not required for Samoan purposes in the standard IC fact pattern because distributions are free of Samoan WHT. Where a treaty partner grants foreign tax credit relief, the IC should obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Ministry for Revenue: the application requires the certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, registered agent confirmation, and a declaration of the IC's management-and-control location; issuance typically takes 5–7 working days. If a residual Samoan WHT is ever assessed (where the exemption is lost), the non-resident recipient invokes DTA relief by filing a withholding tax reduction claim with the Ministry for Revenue using Form P-NR, attaching the TRC, the DTA article analysis, and the underlying franchise or loan agreement; processing takes 15–30 working days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory ceiling for ordinary resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2012 is 15% on royalties and 15% on interest paid to non-residents. A tax-exempt Samoa IC does not deduct any WHT on franchise royalties, syrup supply payments, trademark licence fees, or intercompany loans. Under the Australia and New Zealand DTAs, treaty rates for royalties and interest are generally 10%, and for dividends 5%–15% depending on shareholding, but treaty relief is practically irrelevant for IC outbound flows that are already Samoan tax-exempt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory WST threshold is published in Samoa under the Income Tax Act 2012 transfer pricing provisions; the arm's length standard applies to resident CIT taxpayers without a mandatory Samoan Local File or Master File filing requirement. The exempt IC has no Samoan TP documentation obligation. Group-level Master File, Local File, and CbCR obligations arise only in the parent group's jurisdiction (e.g., group revenue above the OECD CbCR threshold of approximately USD 850 million), where the intercompany royalty charged by the Samoa IC to boba tea franchisees must be supported by a global benchmarking study, franchise valuation model, and contemporaneous substance documentation.
